title: CI-driven release orchestrator with keyed attestation and staged promotion
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a CI-driven orchestrator that creates build artifacts for new model checkpoints, produces cryptographic attestations using a keyed signer (KMS/HSM-backed), runs performance/quality validation against a baseline profile, and automatically stages promotion to canary and full release if checks pass. This ticket covers pipeline orchestration, artifact manifest format, signing flow, verification hooks, promotion API, rollback tombstone, and basic observability for the release path.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline creates reproducible model artifact tarball and performance profile manifest
Artifact manifest is cryptographically signed by the KMS-backed signer and stored in the artifact registry
Automated perf gating job compares new profile to baseline and emits pass/fail with metrics
Promotion API can mark an artifact as canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% via staged rollout configuration
Runtime rejects unsanctioned model versions if signature verification fails
Rollback path can tombstone a release and automatically revert traffic routing
Dashboard shows sign_time, verify_time, gate_result, and promotion_latency
tasks: Define manifest schema (model hashes, build metadata, perf profile pointers, provenance) and land spec
Add CI build step to produce deterministic artifact and upload to registry
Implement keyed-attestation service integration with cloud KMS / HSM
Add verification step in runtime that consults attestation broker before exposing model
Create perf-gate job that runs benchmark suite and compares against baseline thresholds
Build promotion controller (API + small service) that changes pin bindings in model-catalog
Add observability metrics and a lightweight dashboard for release health
Write runbook for rollback and incident flow when a promoted model has regressions
comments: 2025-11-05 - Aisha Khan: Spiked manifest schema with fields for artifact_hash, model_arch, build_env, perf_profile_ref, signer_key_id. Decided to embed a minimal provenance block to keep verification cheap on the runtime. Added initial acceptance criteria.

2025-11-08 - Miguel Ortega: POC for signer integration against cloud KMS is working. KMS Sign API latency ~120ms per sign; decided we will sign asynchronously in pipeline to avoid blocking job lands. Need to confirm HSM key rotation policy with Security.

2025-11-10 - Security (R. Patel): Reviewed signer approach. Recommended KMS key usage with rotation and attestation records stored in vault. Marked security_review_required. Also suggested adding nonce and build_id in manifest to avoid replay.

2025-11-12 - Miguel Ortega: Perf gate prototype runs three workloads (latency p50/p95, throughput at target batch sizes, prompt-quality eval set) and outputs JSON with diff percentages vs baseline. Observed a 3.8% latency regression on long-context workloads for the quantized build. Flagged as tolerable for canary but must fail full promotion if >5%.

2025-11-15 - PM (Zoe Martin): Suggest adding a manual approval step before 50% promotion for enterprise customers. Also requested that the promotion controller publish a changelog entry with artifact metadata.

2025-11-17 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented promotion controller API and wired catalog pin updates to a controlled broadcast. Integration tests added. Next: implement runtime verification hook and dashboard panels.
notes: Trade-offs: synchronous signing in CI would provide stronger immediate guarantees but increases pipeline latency. We chose async signing with a verification step before promotion to keep developer feedback fast.
Rollout policy: default staged promotion is 10% -> 50% -> 100% with a 2-hour observation window. Customers on Dedicated can opt for stricter checks or manual approval.

Observability: minimal metric set = model_release_sign_time_seconds, model_release_verify_success_total, perf_gate_pass_total, promotion_step_duration_seconds. Dashboards to reuse existing release-health panels.
Future: correlate perf gate results with user-facing error budgets and automatic canary rollback if user traffic P99 errors increase above threshold.
